project.name: Showpass
project.footer: Source of truth: the SQL files in `db/migrations/`. This is a synthetic example schema that ships with the plugin; no real company's data is described here.

labels.softDeleteWhy: The row is hidden straight away (`deleted_at`). The nightly purge job removes it for good after 30 days.

badges.stored counts: A running total kept on the row so the ticket page doesn't count rows on every view. Moved by the checkout transaction, repaired nightly.
badges.soft delete: Deleting sets `deleted_at` and hides the row. Nothing is removed until the purge job runs.

highlight.label: new
highlight.note: Added in migration 014 (the waitlist and mobile check-in release).

areas.name: Organizations & people
areas.desc: Who sells tickets, and who may act for them.

areas.name: Venues & seating
areas.desc: Where an event happens, and how the room is split up.

areas.name: Events & tickets on sale
areas.desc: What is for sale: the event, its sessions, its ticket types and its codes.

areas.name: Orders & tickets sold
areas.desc: A basket becomes an order, and an order becomes tickets with names on them.

areas.name: At the door
areas.desc: Scanning on the night, and the queue for sold-out tickets.

areas.name: Money in and out
areas.desc: Charges from buyers, refunds back to them, and payouts to organizers.

areas.name: Messaging & audit
areas.desc: What the platform sent, what it tried to send, and who changed what.

attendees.purpose: One row per ticket, with the name that will be checked at the door.

columns.event_id: Copied from the order so door scanning never has to join through `orders`
columns.order_id: With `line_no`, the order line this ticket was bought on
columns.line_no: Part of the link to `order_lines`, not a number the buyer sees
columns.email: Where this ticket was sent. NULL when the buyer kept all tickets in their own name
columns.barcode: Printed on the ticket and scanned at the door. Unique across every event
columns.seat_label: Set only for `reserved` ticket types; NULL for general admission
columns.status: `transferred` means the name changed, not that the ticket moved order
columns.transferred_at: Last time the name on the ticket was changed

notes: Buying three tickets on one line creates three rows here, one per seat.
Changing the name on a ticket updates this row. The order and its totals never change.

audit_log.purpose: One row per change an organizer or admin made.

columns.actor_user_id: NULL for changes made by a background job or by support tooling
columns.entity_type: Table name, as written in the migrations
columns.entity_id: The row's `id` in `entity_type`. Deliberately not a foreign key, so the log outlives the row
columns.before: The changed columns only, not the whole row
columns.after: The changed columns only, not the whole row
columns.ip: Of the request that made the change, when there was one

notes: Append only. Nothing in the application updates or deletes a row here.

check_ins.purpose: One row per scan at the door, including the scans that were turned away.

columns.checked_in_by: The door staff member. NULL once their account is deleted
columns.device_label: Whatever the scanning app calls itself, e.g. `Gate B iPad`
columns.result: Only `ok` lets someone in. The rest are kept so the door can be audited

notes: A failed scan is a row too. Counting people in means counting `result = 'ok'`.
`event_id` is denormalised from `attendees` so the door query stays on one table.

discount_codes.purpose: One row per code a buyer can type at checkout.

columns.event_id: NULL for a code that works on every event the organization sells
columns.code: Compared case-insensitively by the application; stored as typed
columns.amount_off_cents: Set only when `kind = 'amount'`, in the order's currency
columns.redemption_count: Raised inside the checkout transaction, so two buyers can't pass the limit

event_sessions.purpose: One row per sitting of an event that runs more than once.

columns.seating_zone_id: Set when the session only uses part of the venue
columns.position: Display order; the application renumbers from 0 on every save

notes: A single-sitting event has no row here. Nothing is sold per session yet.

events.purpose: One row per event on sale.

columns.created_by: The organizer who first saved it. NULL once their account is deleted
columns.slug: Used in the public URL, unique inside the organization
columns.status: `sold_out` is set by the checkout job, not by hand
columns.timezone: IANA name. All the timestamps are absolute; this is how they are shown
columns.cancelled_at: Set together with `status = 'cancelled'`; refunds are queued from here

notes: An event can't be deleted while an organization still exists for it, and the organization can't be deleted while it has events.
Cancelling is not deleting: the row stays so tickets, payments and refunds still make sense.

notifications.purpose: One row per message the platform sent to one person.

columns.event_id: What the message was about. Cleared if the event is deleted, which keeps the send record
columns.status: `skipped` means the person had turned this message off
columns.error: Provider message for a `failed` send, kept for support

order_lines.purpose: One row per ticket type in an order, with how many were bought.

columns.line_no: Numbered from 1 inside the order, and never reused
columns.unit_price_cents: The price at the moment of checkout, not today's price
columns.line_total_cents: `unit_price_cents × quantity`, stored so historic orders never move

notes: Editing a paid order is not allowed. A mistake is refunded and bought again.

orders.purpose: One row per basket, which becomes a purchase once it is paid.

columns.user_id: NULL for guest checkout, which is most orders
columns.discount_code_id: Cleared if the code is deleted; `discount_cents` keeps the money that was taken off
columns.buyer_email: Where the tickets were sent. The only way to find a guest order
columns.status: `cart` rows are not purchases and are excluded from every report
columns.subtotal_cents: Sum of the order lines, before discount and fee
columns.fee_cents: The platform's cut, taken from `organizations.fee_bps` at checkout
columns.total_cents: What the buyer was charged. The database checks it against the other three
columns.placed_at: Set when the basket is submitted; NULL while `status = 'cart'`
columns.expires_at: When an unpaid basket releases its held tickets

notes: A basket is a row here from the first ticket added, so held stock is visible to everyone.
Abandoned baskets are swept hourly: `status` becomes `expired` and the held quantities go back.

org_members.purpose: One row per person who may act for an organization.

columns.role: What this person may do in the organizer dashboard
columns.invited_by: Who sent the invitation. NULL once that account is deleted
columns.accepted_at: NULL while the invitation is still outstanding

notes: No surrogate key: the pair of ids is the primary key, so one person can hold one role per organization.

organizations.purpose: One row per organizer account that sells tickets.

columns.parent_org_id: Set for a venue group's sub-accounts, which share billing. NULL for a standalone organizer
columns.slug: Used in the public URL and unique across the whole platform
columns.plan: Decides the feature flags, not the fee
columns.payout_currency: Payouts are made in this currency; events may still sell in another
columns.fee_bps: Platform fee in basis points, copied onto each order at checkout
columns.deleted_at: Hides the organization. Events, orders and payments are kept

notes: The tenant root: almost everything else is reachable from a row here.

payments.purpose: One row per attempt to charge a buyer.

columns.payout_batch_id: Set when the payment is swept into a payout. NULL until then
columns.provider_charge_id: The processor's own id, unique per provider. NULL for an attempt that never reached them
columns.status: `disputed` is set from a provider webhook and never by the application
columns.failure_code: The provider's code for a `failed` attempt

notes: A failed attempt stays. An order can have several rows here and at most one that succeeded.
Nothing here is ever deleted: both the order and the organization refuse to go while payments exist.

payout_batches.purpose: One row per transfer of takings to an organizer.

columns.period_start: First day of takings in this batch, inclusive
columns.period_end: Last day of takings in this batch, inclusive
columns.gross_cents: Sum of the successful payments swept into the batch
columns.fee_cents: Sum of the platform fees on those payments
columns.net_cents: What was actually sent. The database checks it against the other two
columns.status: `sent` means handed to the bank; `paid` means the bank confirmed it

refunds.purpose: One row per amount sent back to a buyer.

columns.order_id: Carried so refunds can be totalled per order without joining `payments`
columns.requested_by: The staff member who asked for it. NULL for an automatic refund after a cancellation
columns.amount_cents: May be less than the payment: partial refunds are normal

notes: Several partial refunds against one payment are allowed. The application keeps their sum within the payment.

seating_zones.purpose: One row per named part of a venue, such as a stand or a tier.

columns.capacity: Seats in this zone. The sum across zones may be below the venue's own `capacity`
columns.position: Display order; the application renumbers from 0 on every save

notes: Deleting a zone leaves its ticket types and sessions in place with an empty zone.

ticket_types.purpose: One row per thing a buyer can put in a basket.

columns.seating_zone_id: Set for `reserved` types. Cleared if the zone is deleted
columns.kind: Decides whether a seat label is assigned and whether money is taken
columns.price_cents: `0` for `comp` tickets, which still create attendees
columns.quantity_total: How many may ever be sold, including the ones already sold
columns.quantity_sold: Raised inside the checkout transaction; the database refuses to let it pass `quantity_total`
columns.max_per_order: Per-basket cap shown on the ticket page
columns.sales_start_at: NULL means on sale as soon as the event is published
columns.sales_end_at: NULL means on sale until the event starts
columns.position: Display order on the ticket page; renumbered from 0 on every save

notes: Price and name can change. Sold orders keep their own copy, so changing them never moves a past total.

user_devices.purpose: One row per phone or browser signed in for push messages.

columns.platform: Which push service the token belongs to
columns.push_token: The provider's token. Unique across the platform, because the provider reissues it
columns.label: Device name the person can recognise in their settings
columns.last_seen_at: Last time the app opened. Tokens unused for 90 days are deleted

users.purpose: One row per person with a sign-in, whether buyer or organizer.

columns.email: Unique case-insensitively, through a unique index on `lower(email)`
columns.locale: Which language messages are sent in
columns.password_set_at: NULL for an account that has only ever used a magic link
columns.deleted_at: Hides the account. Orders and tickets stay, with the link cleared

notes: Most buyers never have a row here: guest checkout only stores `orders.buyer_email`.

venues.purpose: One row per place an organization puts events on.

columns.timezone: IANA name, used to show times for events held here
columns.capacity: Whole-venue limit. NULL when nobody has filled it in
columns.latitude: Set by geocoding the address, not typed in
columns.longitude: Set by geocoding the address, not typed in

notes: A venue can't be deleted while an event still points at it.

waitlist_entries.purpose: One row per person waiting for a ticket that is sold out.

columns.ticket_type_id: NULL to wait for any ticket type, or cleared when that type is deleted
columns.user_id: NULL when someone joined the waitlist without signing in
columns.email: One entry per email per event
columns.expires_at: When an offer lapses and the stock goes to the next person

notes: The release job walks `status = 'waiting'` in `created_at` order, oldest first.

webhook_deliveries.purpose: One row per webhook the platform tried to deliver to an organizer's endpoint.

columns.event_name: Which platform event this payload describes
columns.target_url: Copied from the endpoint's settings at send time, so the history stays true
columns.payload: Exactly what was sent, including the signature header's body
columns.attempt_count: Retries back off; the sender gives up after 8
columns.response_code: HTTP status of the last attempt. NULL if the request never completed

notes: Rows older than 30 days are deleted by the nightly job.

audit_log.action.note: This list lives in `app/services/audit.rb`, not in the database. The column accepts any text, so a typo is stored happily.

notifications.channel.note: Set from the `Channel` union in `app/notifications/`. The database accepts any text.

hints.event_cancelled: Written by the cancellation job, not by a person
hints.fraud: Also closes the order and voids its attendees

refunds.reason.note: Application list, from `app/models/refund.rb`. The database does not restrict it.

webhook_deliveries.event_name.note: The published webhook catalogue, from `app/webhooks/catalogue.rb`. New names are added here as features ship; the database accepts any text.

indexes.attendees_event_email_idx: Find a buyer's tickets at the door when they have lost the barcode
indexes.attendees_ticket_type_idx: Keeps the `restrict` check on ticket types cheap
indexes.audit_log_entity_idx: The history panel on one row, newest first
indexes.check_ins_event_scanned_idx: The live door feed during an event
indexes.check_ins_one_ok_per_attendee: Stops the same ticket being admitted twice, even from two gates at once
indexes.discount_codes_live_idx: The codes a checkout may still accept
indexes.events_on_sale_idx: The public listing of what is on sale next
indexes.events_org_starts_idx: The organizer dashboard: our events, soonest first
indexes.order_lines_ticket_type_idx: Keeps the `restrict` check on ticket types cheap
indexes.orders_buyer_email_lower_idx: Support looking up a guest order by email
indexes.orders_event_placed_idx: An event's sales list, newest first, baskets excluded
indexes.orders_expiring_carts_idx: The sweeper that releases held tickets
indexes.org_members_user_idx: Which organizations one person can act for
indexes.organizations_live_idx: Resolving a slug from the public URL
indexes.payments_order_idx: Every attempt against one order, for the support view
indexes.payments_unbatched_idx: What the next payout batch should sweep up
indexes.ticket_types_available_idx: The ticket page: what is still buyable, in display order
indexes.user_devices_user_idx: The push tokens for one person, most recent first
indexes.users_last_seen_idx: Recently active accounts, for support and for the activity report
indexes.waitlist_entries_waiting_idx: The release job: who is next for this event

tour.title: The database in one sentence
text: One PostgreSQL database runs the whole ticketing platform: **{tables} tables**, grouped into **{areas} areas**.
Read it as a shop. An organizer lists an event, a buyer fills a basket, money moves, and someone scans a barcode at the door.

tour.title: Everything belongs to an organization
text: `organizations` is the tenant. {in:organizations} links from {inFrom:organizations} tables point to it, more than to any other table.
`org_members` says who may act for one. It has no id of its own: the pair of organization and user *is* the key, so one person holds one role per organization.

tour.title: An organization can own another one
text: `organizations.parent_org_id` points back at `organizations`. A venue group uses it for its sub-accounts, which share billing.
Delete a parent and the children stay, with `parent_org_id` cleared. Nothing cascades.

tour.title: Where an event happens
text: A venue belongs to one organization. `seating_zones` splits the room into named parts, which reserved ticket types point at.
Deleting a venue is refused while any event still points at it. Deleting the organization takes its venues with it.

tour.title: An event's life
text: `events.status` is the one column that decides whether the public can see the event and whether tickets can be bought.
`cancelled` can be reached from any step, and is never a delete: the row has to survive so its tickets and payments still make sense.

tour.title: What an event sells
text: `ticket_types` is the thing a buyer actually puts in a basket: a name, a price and a quantity. `event_sessions` only exists for events that run more than once.
`discount_codes` can hang off one event or off the whole organization.

tour.title: A basket becomes an order
text: A basket is a real `orders` row from the first ticket added, so held stock is visible to everyone. `status = 'cart'` keeps it out of every report.
`order_lines` has a composite primary key: `(order_id, line_no)`. Line numbers start at 1 inside an order and are never reused.

tour.title: One row per ticket, with a name on it
text: Buying three tickets on one line creates three `attendees` rows. That is where the barcode lives, and the only id the door app ever sees.
`attendees` points at `order_lines` with **two** columns at once, because the line it came from needs both.

tour.title: What happens when something is deleted
text: Every link says what happens to a row when the row it points at is deleted. There are three answers, and the schema uses all three.

visual.cascade: An event's ticket types, sessions and attendees go with it. {cascade} links work this way.
visual.setnull: A deleted staff account leaves its check-ins in place with `checked_in_by` empty. {setnull} links.
visual.restrict: An order with a payment against it refuses to be deleted. {restrict} links.

tour.title: Money in, money out
text: `payments` is one row per *attempt*, so a failed card is a row too. At most one of them succeeded.
`refunds` can be partial and can be several per payment. `payout_batches` sweeps succeeded payments into one transfer to the organizer.

tour.title: At the door, and in the queue
text: `check_ins` records every scan, including the ones turned away, so a disputed night can be read back. A unique index allows only one `ok` scan per ticket.
`waitlist_entries` is the queue for a sold-out type. An offer holds stock until it expires, then moves to the next person.

tour.title: Where to go next
text: `notifications`, `webhook_deliveries` and `audit_log` are the platform's own record of what it sent and who changed what. None of them is read by the app itself.
Explore walks the areas table by table. Reference has every link, every index and every rule in one list.

reference.title: Conventions
reference.desc: The patterns nearly every table follows

items.title: Internal keys
items.text: `id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`. For joins only, and **never sent to a client**.

items.title: Public keys
items.text: `public_id uuid` on every row a client can name, so nothing can be guessed or counted from a URL.

items.title: Slugs
items.text: `organizations.slug` and `events.slug` name those rows in public URLs. Event slugs are unique inside the organization, not globally.

items.title: Money
items.text: Integer cents plus a `char(3)` currency on the same row. No floats anywhere, and no implied currency.

items.title: Timestamps
items.text: `timestamptz`, always absolute. `events.timezone` and `venues.timezone` say how to show them. `updated_at` is set by the application, not by a trigger.

items.title: Status columns
items.text: `text` with `CHECK (… IN (…))`, so the database rejects an unknown value. The same lists are generated into `app/types/status.ts` by `rake schema:types`.

items.title: Soft delete
items.text: `deleted_at` on `organizations` and `users` only. Everything else is deleted for real or cancelled in place.

items.title: Stored counts
items.text: `ticket_types.quantity_sold` and `discount_codes.redemption_count` are moved inside the checkout transaction and repaired nightly. A CHECK stops `quantity_sold` passing `quantity_total`.

items.title: Denormalised ids
items.text: `attendees.event_id`, `check_ins.event_id` and `refunds.order_id` repeat an id that could be joined for. They exist so the door app and the finance reports stay on one table.

items.title: Ordered children
items.text: `position` on `event_sessions`, `seating_zones` and `ticket_types`. Renumbered from 0 on every save, in one statement.

items.title: Polymorphic references
items.text: `audit_log.entity_type` and `audit_log.entity_id` have no foreign key on purpose, so the log outlives the rows it describes.

items.title: Cents, not currency maths
items.text: Totals are checked by the database: `orders.total_cents` against its three parts, `order_lines.line_total_cents` against unit price and quantity, `payout_batches.net_cents` against gross and fees.

reference.title: How data changes and expires
reference.desc: Status flows, the jobs that move them, and what is cleaned up

items.title: An event
items.text: `cancelled` is reachable from any step. `sold_out` is set by the checkout job when the last ticket type fills, and back to `on_sale` when a refund frees stock.

items.title: An order
items.text: Then `partially_refunded` or `refunded` as money goes back. `cancelled` is for an organizer cancelling, `expired` for the basket sweeper.

items.title: A ticket
items.text: `transferred` means the name changed. `void` is set by a full refund or by a fraud case, and a void ticket is refused at the door.

items.title: A waitlist entry
items.text: `expired` when an offer is not taken before `expires_at`. The stock then moves to the next `waiting` row.

sections.title: Jobs that write to the database

items.title: Basket sweeper
items.text: Hourly. Sets `orders.status = 'expired'` past `expires_at` and lowers `ticket_types.quantity_sold` by what the basket held.

items.title: Waitlist release
items.text: Every five minutes. Offers freed stock to the oldest `waiting` entry and queues a notification.

items.title: Payout sweep
items.text: Weekly. Opens a `payout_batches` row per organization and sets `payments.payout_batch_id` on the succeeded payments inside the period.

items.title: Count repair
items.text: Nightly. Recounts `ticket_types.quantity_sold` and `discount_codes.redemption_count` from the orders and corrects any drift.

items.title: Purge
items.text: Nightly. Removes `organizations` and `users` rows soft-deleted more than 30 days ago, `webhook_deliveries` older than 30 days, and `user_devices` unused for 90 days.

sections.title: What survives a delete
sections.note: Deleting a `users` row clears `orders.user_id` but keeps the order, its lines, its attendees and its payments. The buyer's email stays on the order, because a guest order has nothing else to find it by.

items.title: Deleting an organization
items.text: Refused while it has events, orders, payments or payout batches. In practice organizations are soft-deleted instead.

items.title: Deleting an event
items.text: Takes its sessions, ticket types, discount codes, attendees, check-ins and waitlist with it. Refused while it has orders.

items.title: Deleting an order
items.text: Takes its lines and their attendees and check-ins. Refused while a payment or refund points at it.

reference.desc: Every foreign key ({links}) and what deleting does

reference.title: Indexes
reference.desc: What is indexed, and for which screen
